newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poll shows French Socialists win race for trust.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows French Socialists win race for trust.

text.p: French voters, facing a snap election next month, have slightly more faith in the opposition Socialist party to address France's problems than in either party of the ruling coalition, an opinion poll said on Tuesday.

The survey, by the BVA institute for BFM radio, showed that 34 percent of voters reckoned the Socialists could "offer a policy to improve the economic and social situation of France", down one point from a similar poll last month.

The Socialist scored slightly better than Prime Minister Alain Juppe's Rally for the Republic (RPR) party on 29 percent, down four points. The junior partner in his coalition, the Union for French Democracy (UDF), scored 25 percent, also down four and level with the tiny Ecologist party.

The survey of 968 people was conducted on April 18 and 19, at the height of speculation on whether President Jacques Chirac would call a snap parliamentary election, which Chirac said on Monday would be held on May 25 and June 1, more than nine months early.

Curiously, the poll found that for each party, the number of voters responding "don't know" increased from the previous month, an effect which might be due to voters questioning their existing political preferences in light of the speculation about early elections.
According to the poll, which did not ask about voting intentions, the Communist Party was on 18 percent and the National Front last with 13 percent.
A separate BVA poll for the daily Le Monde showed that 54 percent of voters named cutting unemployment as the first priority for the government.

Other issues, such as reducing economic insecurity, fighting drugs, ensuring housing and cutting the social security deficit, were mentioned as top priorities only by a handful of voters. The Le Monde poll was taken on April 4 and 5 among 955 people.

Voters in the BVA poll were asked to say in light of the forthcoming parliamentary election which of the following political parties offered policies to improve the social and economic situation in France

The BVA polling institute said the poll was carried out using a representative sample of the French population aged 18 and over. Some 968 people were polled by telephone on April 18 and 19, 1997. Sampling by quotas for gender, age, professional category and geographical criteria. The poll carries a margin of error of plus or minus two to three points.
